task: Add remembered Find/Replace history to the Form Field Find & Replace Firefox extension: (1) remember previous Find and Replace values and show them in a dropdown when the Find/Replace fields are clicked, (2) remember the search settings (regex, match case, whole word, include-iframes, field-type selections) associated with each remembered pair and restore them when an entry is selected, (3) expand the popup dialog so all elements display without vertical scrolling. Constraints: manifest permissions stay exactly ["activeTab","scripting","storage"] with no host_permissions and no network calls; no innerHTML/eval/Function( anywhere in popup/ or content/ (createElement/textContent only for the new dropdown); storage.local only, never storage.sync; history storage must be bounded; the existing restoreState() race (a prior bug: restoreState overwriting typed input) must not be reintroduced; the dropdown must be keyboard-accessible and automation-friendly (stable ids/data-testid, accessible names/roles); Firefox popups cap at 800x600, so the sizing fix must be a layout/density change, not just taller CSS; all 88 existing Playwright tests and 8 existing Selenium tests must keep passing unweakened.

phases.name: Design decision + red-baseline regression tests
phases.description: Record the history design decisions in writing (shared paired-entry list vs two independent lists, storage key, bound, save-trigger, dedup/eviction rule, dropdown positioning strategy), then write new Playwright tests against that decided shape that fail against the current, unmodified popup/popup.js and popup/popup.html.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision exists (as a code comment block at the top of the new history section of popup/popup.js, or a dedicated section in README.md/SPEC.md) stating explicitly: history is ONE shared list of paired entries (find value + replace value + the four option flags [matchCase, wholeWord, regex, includeIframes] + the full fieldTypes selection map) captured together, not two independent find-only/replace-only lists -- selecting any entry restores the whole pair plus its settings

The same written decision names: the storage.local key used for history (distinct from the existing STORAGE_KEY='formFieldFindReplace' state key, e.g. 'formFieldFindReplaceHistory', so history and last-typed-state remain independently readable/clearable), the maximum entry count (a fixed integer, e.g. 20), the eviction rule when the bound is exceeded (oldest evicted, FIFO, OR most-recently-used semantics with move-to-front on exact-duplicate re-save -- pick one and state it), and the save trigger (a new entry is recorded only when Count matches or Replace all is invoked with a non-empty find value -- not on every keystroke, to avoid saving typing noise)

The written decision states the dropdown's positioning strategy: the history listbox for each input is an absolutely-positioned overlay anchored under that input (not inserted into normal document flow), specifically so opening it does not increase the popup document's scrollHeight -- this is load-bearing for phase 4's no-overflow requirement, not a cosmetic choice

A new Playwright test file (e.g. test/history-dropdown.spec.js) exists under C:\Users\mhasse\source\FF_replace\test\, following the addInitScript-mocked-browser-and-storage mounting pattern already used in test/undo.spec.js and test/activation.spec.js

The new file contains at least these failing-by-design test cases against current code: (a) after invoking Replace all (or Count) with a non-empty find value via the mocked flow, storage.local under the decided history key contains a new entry with the find/replace/options/fieldTypes recorded; (b) clicking the find input renders a visible listbox (role='listbox') of prior entries built via createElement (asserted by inspecting the live DOM, not by string-matching HTML source) with stable ids/data-testid attributes on both the listbox container and each option row; (c) selecting a rendered history entry (by click and separately by keyboard Enter after ArrowDown navigation) restores find, replace, matchCase, wholeWord, regex, includeIframes, and at least one non-default field-type checkbox state to that entry's saved values; (d) saving more than the decided max entry count leaves storage.local's history array length capped at that max, with the correct entries evicted per the documented eviction rule

Running `npx playwright test test/history-dropdown.spec.js` against the current unmodified popup/popup.js and popup/popup.html produces at least 3 failing tests (documented with test name + failure reason in the phase's completion evidence), proving these are not vacuous pass-either-way tests
No file under C:\Users\mhasse\source\FF_replace\popup\ or C:\Users\mhasse\source\FF_replace\content\ is modified in this phase -- only new test files and documentation

phases.name: History persistence layer
phases.description: Implement the bounded, paired-entry history storage layer in popup/popup.js per phase 1's written decision -- new storage key, save/load/prune functions wired into the existing Count/Replace-all action handlers -- without yet building the visible dropdown UI, and turn the phase-1 storage/bounding tests green.
acceptance_criteria: popup/popup.js defines a history storage key distinct from STORAGE_KEY (matching phase 1's documented name), a MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES constant matching the documented bound, and functions to load history from storage.local, append/dedup a new paired entry, and persist the pruned array back to storage.local -- using storage.local exclusively (grep confirms no storage.sync usage anywhere in the diff)

handleCount() and handleReplaceAll() in popup/popup.js record a new history entry (find, replace, options, fieldTypes) only when the find value is non-empty at the moment the action runs, matching the documented save trigger -- no history entry is written on every keystroke/input event

The append logic enforces the documented bound: saving beyond MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES evicts per the documented rule (verified by the phase-1 bounding test (d) now passing) rather than growing storage.local without limit

Every new field written to storage.local is built with primitive string/boolean/object values only -- no functions, no DOM nodes -- consistent with storage.local's structured-clone requirement and the threat model's 'attacker-influenced remembered text' note (a remembered find/replace value may contain arbitrary text copied from a page; it is stored as inert string data, never interpreted)

The phase-1 storage/bounding test cases (a) and (d) in test/history-dropdown.spec.js now pass; the dropdown-rendering and entry-selection test cases (b) and (c) are still expected to fail at this point (no UI yet) and that is documented as expected, not silently ignored
`bash security-audit.sh` exits 0 against the modified working tree (permissions allowlist unchanged, no eval/innerHTML/Function( introduced, no host_permissions added)

phases.name: Keyboard-accessible history dropdown UI
phases.description: Build the createElement/textContent-only history dropdown for the Find and Replace inputs -- ARIA combobox/listbox pattern, mouse and keyboard operable, stable automation-friendly ids -- wired so selecting an entry restores the full paired state without racing or reintroducing the restoreState()-overwrites-typed-input bug, and turn the remaining phase-1 UI tests green.
acceptance_criteria: popup/popup.html and popup/popup.js gain a history listbox associated with each of #find-input and #replace-input, built entirely via document.createElement/appendChild/textContent -- grep of the diff and of the final popup/popup.js and popup/popup.html confirm zero occurrences of `.innerHTML =` (security-audit.sh's dangerous_code_scan already fails the build on this; this criterion is the same check applied explicitly to the new code)

Each listbox and each rendered option row carries a stable id and data-testid attribute (e.g. #find-history-listbox / [data-testid='find-history-listbox'], and per-row ids/data-testids incorporating a stable index), and the trigger input has role='combobox', aria-expanded, and aria-controls pointing at the listbox id, and the listbox itself has role='listbox' with role='option' rows -- verifiable by reading the rendered DOM in a Playwright test, not by eyeballing markup

The dropdown opens on click/focus of the associated input and is operable by keyboard alone: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move a visually and programmatically indicated active option (aria-activedescendant or equivalent), Enter selects the active option and closes the dropdown, and Escape closes the dropdown WITHOUT triggering the existing global Escape handler's cancel-run-or-close-popup behavior (i.e. Escape's effect while the dropdown is open is scoped to the dropdown first, verified by a test that opens the dropdown, presses Escape, and asserts the popup is still open and no run was cancelled)

Selecting an entry (by click or by keyboard) restores find, replace, matchCase, wholeWord, regex, includeIframes, and all fieldTypes checkboxes to that entry's saved values in a single synchronous update, then persists the restored state via the existing persistState() path -- reusing the existing applyState()-style assignment logic rather than a second duplicated restore implementation

The dropdown wiring does not reintroduce the restoreState() race: the dropdown's click/focus listeners and any history-driven restore are attached only after init()'s `await restoreState()` has resolved, and opening the dropdown or selecting an entry never runs concurrently with an in-flight restoreState() call, verified by a Playwright test that triggers a click on the find input immediately after popup mount and asserts the typed/restored value is never transiently overwritten
Phase-1 test cases (b) and (c) in test/history-dropdown.spec.js now pass; test cases (a) and (d) from phase 2 still pass (no regression)
`bash security-audit.sh` exits 0 against the modified working tree

phases.name: No-scroll popup layout
phases.description: Rework popup/popup.css (and popup/popup.html structure if needed) so every element is visible without vertical scrolling across all disclosure states, within Firefox's 800x600 popup cap, using layout density changes (e.g. a multi-column field-type grid, tighter vertical rhythm, the phase-1-documented absolutely-positioned dropdown overlay) rather than simply increasing height -- backed by a mechanical Playwright measurement, not a visual eyeball check.
acceptance_criteria: A new or extended Playwright test (e.g. test/popup-layout.spec.js or an added block in test/history-dropdown.spec.js) asserts `document.documentElement.scrollHeight <= document.documentElement.clientHeight` (or the equivalent body measurement) with zero tolerance for vertical overflow, at the popup's declared CSS width, for EACH of these distinct states in the same test file: (1) default mount with the field-types section expanded (its default state) and no status/error text, (2) the undo-cap warning banner (#undo-warning) visible with its longest realistic message, (3) the status line (#status-line) showing its longest realistic message (a multi-part Replaced/skipped/timedOut string), (4) the find-input history dropdown open showing at least 5 entries, (5) the field-types section expanded AND the history dropdown open simultaneously (the worst-case combination)

The popup's total rendered height in every one of the five states stays within Firefox's hard 800x600 popup cap (documented as a comment near the CSS width/height rules explaining why height is bounded and cannot simply grow), and the fix is achieved via layout density (grep/read of popup.css shows a multi-column grid or flex-wrap applied to the field-type checkbox groups, reduced vertical margins/padding, and the history listbox using position:absolute so it does not contribute to document flow height) rather than by only changing a max-height or overflow:auto rule to hide the problem
popup/popup.css's body width is documented (comment) alongside the reasoning for its final value, and the width chosen still fits the 800px cap with margin

No existing #app, #find-replace-form, or field id/data-testid attribute is removed or renamed (only layout/CSS and structural wrapper changes), so no unrelated existing Playwright test breaks from selector changes
All phase-1/2/3 tests in test/history-dropdown.spec.js still pass unmodified, plus the new popup-layout overflow tests all pass

phases.name: Full regression sweep, security audit, and documentation
phases.description: Run the complete Playwright and Selenium suites together with the new history/dropdown/layout tests to confirm no regression anywhere, confirm the security policy still holds, update README.md/SPEC.md/CLAUDE.md to describe the new feature and its design decisions, and confirm the extension still builds as an unsigned local .xpi.
acceptance_criteria: `npm test` (full Playwright suite -- the prior 88 tests plus all new history/dropdown/layout tests) reports zero failures, with results written to test-results/gtest-results.xml
`npm run test:selenium` reports all 8 existing Selenium tests passing with no new failures and no test weakened or skipped

`bash security-audit.sh` exits 0 on the final working tree: manifest.json's permissions remain exactly ["activeTab","scripting","storage"], no host_permissions key present, no live eval(/.innerHTML =/Function( in popup/ or content/, and no committed-credential pattern matches
`npm run build:xpi` succeeds locally and produces web-ext-artifacts/ffr.xpi (an unsigned local build only -- this criterion does NOT require AMO signing, a merged PR, or a pushed tag)

README.md and/or SPEC.md gain a section documenting: the shared paired-entry history model, the storage.local key and its bound, the save-trigger rule, the dropdown's ARIA combobox/listbox pattern and keyboard operation, and the popup's width/height layout constraints under Firefox's 800x600 cap -- consistent with CLAUDE.md's existing standard of documenting real data flow (not an aspirational description a grep would disprove)
manifest.json's version field is incremented from 0.4.0 to reflect the new feature (e.g. 0.5.0), consistent with the existing build:xpi script's version-matching behavior
A `git diff` review confirms no unrelated files were touched and no test was deleted or weakened to make the suite pass
